findings.problem: The API/§9 permits the original owner to retry a still_open handle in a new context; once a retry confirms closure, the close sequence may advance and release the case/shared lock. The FI rows also permit still_open retries but unconditionally require the case lock to remain held until process exit. This makes successful retry behavior and the test oracle disagree. The unknown branch's bounded child exit/reap rule is consistent and is not the finding.
findings.required: Distinguish successful still_open retry (advance close sequence, release locks normally), pending still_open (retain handle and locks, return close_pending for same-owner continuation), and unknown (restart_required; never retry close/unlock; bounded child exit/reap). Apply this to each affected FI row and its restart assertions.
findings.acceptance: Close tests prove confirmed retry success releases locks in normal order; unresolved still_open retains locks and is resumable only by its owner; unknown never retries the OS operation and holds locks until child PID exit is confirmed.

passed: R4 PASS areas for catalog lock identity/bootstrap, case-lock ordering, state capability and docs/41 alignment remain unchanged.
FI-DB-01a/b/c distinguish application rw opens from bounded read-only recovery checks.
FI-CLEAN-01 enumerates legal source states and zero-byte/complete/partial outcomes; absent-directory cleanup verifies and syncs the pinned parent before tombstone.
Unknown close state consistently requires restart_required and bounded dedicated-child termination/reap; no in-process replacement Supervisor is allowed.
